# Draft:Miles/Dennis Forward Control 88-inch Land Rovers

----
The Alfred Miles/Dennis Forward Control 88-inch Land Rovers were a small group of forward-control specialist vehicles developed between approximately 1959 and 1963. They were built using Land Rover Series II 88-inch wheelbase chassis and running gear but were not produced by the Rover Company itself. Instead, they were developed by Alfred Miles Ltd of Brockworth, Gloucestershire, and later marketed by Dennis Brothers following Dennis’s acquisition of Alfred Miles’ fire appliance interests.
Four vehicles are known to have been built: one prototype fire appliance and three subsequent vehicles, comprising one utility pick-up and two fire engines. The two later fire engines were marketed by Dennis as part of the Dennis M Series, with the “M” designation referring to Miles.
Background
Land Rover did not manufacture a forward-control vehicle on the 88-inch wheelbase. During the late 1950s, Alfred Miles Ltd, then part of the Hawker Siddeley Group, developed a compact forward-control design using Land Rover Series II mechanical components. The aim was to produce specialist vehicles, particularly fire appliances, that combined the manoeuvrability of the short-wheelbase Land Rover with improved load space and accessibility.
Alfred Miles Ltd had an established fire appliance business, producing specialist bodies for a range of chassis. In the early 1960s, this business was acquired by Dennis Brothers, who continued to market Miles-derived fire appliances under the Dennis name.
Development
The Miles forward-control design placed the cab over the front axle, allowing a compact overall length while retaining the standard 88-inch wheelbase. The vehicles used Land Rover Series II chassis, axles, suspension, and drivetrain, combined with bespoke cab and bodywork designed by Alfred Miles.
The programme is generally divided into two stages: a single prototype vehicle, followed by a small number of refined derivatives.
Types
Type A: Prototype fire engine
The first vehicle built was a prototype forward-control fire engine, constructed around 1959–1960. It served as a proof-of-concept and was used at the Alfred Miles works on the Brockworth Trading Estate in Gloucestershire.
* Registration: 9290 DD
* Role: Prototype fire appliance
* Builder: Alfred Miles Ltd
The prototype featured a Coventry Climax fire pump and a light-alloy water tank and was demonstrated publicly at fire service events. It is regarded as the first example of the Miles forward-control 88-inch design.
The last known whereabouts of this vehicle were in Gloucestershire.
---
Type B: Production derivatives
Following evaluation of the prototype, a small number of refined vehicles were built using the same basic forward-control layout. These are commonly referred to as Type B vehicles.
Type B Utility / Pick-Up
One utility vehicle with a dropside rear body was produced.
* Original registration: 83 76 AD
* Later registration: NAS 286 (age-related)
* Role: Utility / dropside pick-up
This vehicle spent its working life in municipal service in Brighton and Hove. It was later sold into private ownership, during which time its original registration was transferred as a cherished plate and replaced with an age-related number. The vehicle has been featured in specialist Land Rover publications and was, for a period, believed to be the only surviving example of the Miles 88-inch forward-control design.
The vehicle is currently in private ownership in Cornwall.
---
Type B Fire Engines (Dennis M Series)
Two fire appliances were built to the refined Type B design. By the time these vehicles entered service and were registered for road use, Alfred Miles Ltd had been acquired by Dennis Brothers. Both vehicles were therefore marketed as Dennis M Series fire engines.
SSN 44
* Registration: SSN 44
* Role: Industrial fire appliance
* Operator: Strathleven Bonded Warehouses Ltd, Dunbartonshire
This vehicle served as a private industrial fire engine at Strathleven Bonded Warehouses. It later entered preservation and is currently in private ownership in Cornwall.
REG 999
* Registration: REG 999
* Role: Industrial fire appliance
* Operator: Baker Perkins works fire brigade, Peterborough
REG 999 was supplied to the Baker Perkins works fire brigade and remained associated with Peterborough. It is currently preserved by the Peterborough Volunteer Fire Brigade and is used as a show and display vehicle.
---
Production numbers
Only four Miles/Dennis Forward Control 88-inch Land Rovers are known to have been built:
# One Type A prototype fire engine
# One Type B utility pick-up
# Two Type B fire engines
No evidence has emerged to suggest series production or wider commercial availability.
Survivors
All four known vehicles are believed to survive, either preserved or in private ownership. Their survival has been attributed to specialist industrial use and early recognition of their historical significance.
Legacy
The Miles/Dennis Forward Control 88-inch Land Rovers are notable for being:
* The only known forward-control vehicles built on the Land Rover 88-inch wheelbase
* An example of third-party specialist engineering using Land Rover components
* A transitional design linking Alfred Miles Ltd and Dennis Brothers fire appliance development
They are frequently cited in Land Rover enthusiast literature as among the rarest Land Rover-based vehicles ever constructed.
